objective: Design proposal 01 of 4: Le Comptoir, a package manager for Arch as a shop counter at night. One 1600x1000 dark desktop screen, the FigCraft source, and the rationale.

inputs.tokens: the design-system tokens taken as they are: anthracite #111418, shell white #F7F3ED, muted #A1A6AD, slate #667085, signal orange 100 #FFE5D2 / 300 #FF8E40 / base #FF6A00 / 700 #C95400, royal blue 300 #87A0F4 / base #4169E1
inputs.derivation_rule: no hue outside the tokens was invented: warm dark wood is the anthracite ground with the signal-orange token composited over it at low alpha; blackened brass is signal orange 700 darkened toward the ground; the grain is a slate noise effect blended overlay

the_decision.the_two_axes: sources are the drawers of a permanent wall in the left column; the operations are the three positions of one brass lever on a milled aluminium channel in the right column
the_decision.the_three_shelves: search, installed and updates are the three shelves of the case: two stay pushed back in shadow, the third is pulled out onto the counter and its empty slot is left open and labelled
the_decision.the_third_operation: remove is a verb on a selected package, so it is a button on the detail board with the exact command, not a fourth shelf
the_decision.the_mark: a scallop shell of seven ribs in a metal cup on a brushed aluminium stem, 84px tall in the header, and engraved as a line drawing on the back panel of the case
the_decision.the_compact_list: shown as a possibility, not as a screen: the ROWS control draws both row shapes, and the open ALPM drawer holds a genuine compact list

what_was_built.generator: build.py (emits build.jsonl; every layer is a figcraft command)

how: the PNG was rendered and read back nine times: the noise effect paints grains at full strength (slate over wood, muted over aluminium, blended overlay); the shell's flanks were drawn on the wrong side of the hinge; the ribs overshot the scalloped margin; the cup was narrower than the fan and left a sliver of shell escaping; the till's lever sat on the channel instead of in it; the wood's first pass was opaque and let the front rail show the row behind it

artefacts.note: the rationale: navigation, material, motion, and the second pass
one question for the other three authors
the generator, in the shared build directory
the figcraft command log, in the shared build directory
build and export, one process per file
the figcraft command log the .figcraft was built from
build and export from the run directory
the render, copied into the run record

rules_kept: the Calix application code was not opened, the running application was not started, and no screenshot of it was looked for: the proposal comes from the brief alone
known_gaps: the fonts are system fonts (IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Sans Condensed, IBM Plex Mono); a render on a machine without them falls back
royal blue is not on this screen: it is the identity's alternative accent, and this direction is warm wood and blackened brass, so the screen carries one accent
the compact density is shown as a control and as a legend inside the open drawer, not as a drawn screen
